review.assessment: The change rewrites the audit comparison from `len(source_rows)` to a derived sum of pages in `sink.pages`. Because paging drops the remainder buffer, those rows are never flushed into emitted pages or counted by the new `expected` metric. This silently disables the row-count check rather than addressing why rows are lost.

findings.actual: Audit passes; export contains fewer rows than input
findings.call: `python run.py` with a source file exceeding PAGE_SIZE rows
findings.defect: The audit now compares flushed output against emitted pages instead of the original row count. Since paging drops remainder buffers, those dropped rows are neither written out nor counted in `sink.pages`. This makes `expected == len(written)`, effectively disabling the mismatch check and masking the root cause.
findings.expected: Audit detects missing rows; export contains every input row
